title: Segmentation-aware VPC orchestration Terraform module for private deployments
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Goal: Implement a robust, segmentation-aware Terraform module that provisions VPCs for Redwood Private deployments with explicit subnet segmentation, resilient NAT/IGW topology, VPC endpoints, route table orchestration, and automated health checks + upgrade safe paths. This module should be usable by the Private control-plane and by the on-prem packaging team with minimal per-customer override.

Scope and requirements:
- Provide opinionated defaults and explicit inputs for: control-plane subnets, app (workload) subnets, management subnets, data plane subnets (if present), AZ mapping, CIDR sizing, and optional secondary CIDR support.
- Support both single NAT-per-AZ and central NAT designs via a boolean flag; provide clear trade-offs in docs.
- Create IGW and optional egress-only IGW for IPv6 paths.
- Expose fine-grained configuration for managed VPC endpoints (S3, ECR, SSM, Secrets Manager) with endpoint policy json input as a string.
- Route table orchestration: per-segment route tables, automatic association rules, mutable propagation for centralized NAT failover, and route priority docs.
- Automated health checks and remediation targets for NAT/endpoint reachability: uses a dedicated health-check Lambda (or container) that performs scheduled checks (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/VPC+Health+Checks) and emits to CloudWatch metrics + alerting. Module should optionally wire up those alarms.
- Upgrade/rollout strategy built into module outputs: versioned resource naming, create_before_destroy where safe, and guidance for destructive changes with an automated tfstate migration helper script.
- Terraform compatibility: support >= 1.5, use provider constraints pinned in examples, provide examples for both AWS provider v4 and v5.
- Security: support endpoint policy enforcement, KMS-encrypted flow logs, VPC flow logs to an encrypted S3 bucket or central logging account. Security review required.
- Testing: include Terratest suite definitions, unit-level tf-validate in CI, and a staged workspace apply in a Private canary account before wider rollout.

Design decisions and trade-offs discussed:
- Segmented subnets improve least privilege and observability but increase route table complexity; we adopt per-segment route tables with a small set of canonical associations to keep complexity manageable.
- NAT architecture default: per-AZ NAT Gateways for minimal cross-AZ latency; provide central-NAT option for cost-sensitive customers.
- Endpoint policies are accepted as raw JSON strings to keep the module provider-agnostic (avoid opinionated higher-level DSL that complicates upgrades).

Module inputs (examples documented in README): VPC CIDR, az_list, map_subnets_by_role (string map as JSON), enable_central_nat (bool), endpoint_config (JSON string), enable_flow_logs (bool), flow_logs_kms_key_arn (string), health_check_config (JSON string), tags (map as JSON).

Module outputs: vpc_id, subnet_ids_by_role (JSON string), nat_gateway_ids (CSV string), route_table_ids_by_role (JSON string), endpoints_ids (CSV string), health_check_alarm_arns (CSV string).

Acceptance criteria (high level):
1) Module deploys in a sandbox account with both default and central NAT modes without manual changes.
2) Health checks create CloudWatch metrics and auto-failover triggers (can be toggled off).
3) Upgrades from v0.1 -> v0.2 that change NAT topology can be executed with documented, minimally disruptive steps and no customer VM termination in normal scenarios.
4) TFsec and internal policy checks pass in CI for all examples.
5) Module README includes step-by-step upgrade playbook and Terratest harness references.

Deliverables:
- Terraform module in infra/modules/vpc-segmentation (with comprehensive README and examples).
- Terratest suite + small E2E in private-canary pipeline.
- Confluence design doc detailing routing/segmentation and upgrade playbook (link below).
- PR addressing policy remediation comments and pipeline entries.

Links: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Segmentation-aware+VPC+module, GitHub draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123, CI canary run dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/infra/vpc-module-canary

Notes: Keep module API deliberately small to reduce migration surface. Avoid embedding account-specific values; prefer data sources and provider aliases for cross-account wiring.
